prompt:
A desktop landing page for Pawlio, a marketplace where Egyptian pet businesses get listed and booked, rendered edge to edge as a finished web screen with crisp readable text, no browser window, device or desk around it.

The visitor is a pet shop owner, vet clinic owner or groomer in Cairo deciding whether to join. Real content: headline "Your pet business, on the street every pet owner walks" with its Arabic pair "نشاطك في الشارع اللي كل صاحب حيوان أليف بيمشي فيه"; subline "Stores, clinics and groomers on one app. Pet owners pay in the app before they arrive, and every business is reviewed by our team before it goes live." Primary action "Join Pawlio", secondary "Sign in".

What leads: a calm street wall with three shopfronts side by side, each a working choice: "Pet store / متجر", "Vet clinic / عيادة بيطرية", "Groomer / جرومنج", each with a short line ("Sell products", "Take paid appointments", "Fill your grooming chair") and an "Open your shop" door action. Only the hovered shopfront's sign is lit. Below starts the next section: "How it works" in three painted steps: apply, we review, open for pet owners.

Frame: Pawlio logo and name top left, links "For stores", "For clinics", "For groomers", a language switch "العربية", and "Sign in" top right.

Visual law: a cool pale limewashed wall is the ground; flat enamel sign panels in deep pharmacy green, marigold and oxblood carry the shopfronts, with black and off-white lettering. Hand-painted sign-writer lettering where Arabic and English are set as equals, mirrored across each sign. One sign, one message: calm, generous wall space, not busy, not cartoonish, no paw-print decoration.
